$comment: Every third-party thing OpenDoctrines ships or builds against, and the terms it is under. This file is the single source of truth: NOTICE.md and the third-party half of data/credits.txt are both generated from it by tools/gen_notices.py, and tests/run_all.sh fails if either has drifted. Add the entry here first; the paperwork follows.

commercial_use.$comment: The game's own licence is the project's to change; the map data's is not. This records that every input already permits commercial use, so that decision stays open. tools/check_data_licences.py enforces it and refuses anything NonCommercial, NoDerivatives, copyleft or silent.
commercial_use.statement: The game is free, and its own licence is the project's to change at any time. This section is about the other half of that question: every third-party dataset and every piece of artwork that reaches a shipped `.odmap` is under terms that already permit commercial use, so releasing the maps commercially would need no renegotiation and no dataset replaced. Two datasets were dropped rather than shipped on a citation request with no grant — see "Data deliberately not used" below.
obligations: **World Bank Open Data** is CC BY 4.0: the attribution below must ship with the game, which it does, in `data/credits.txt` and here.

**Seven flag images** are CC BY-SA. Commercial use is permitted; the share-alike binds those images, so a *modified* version of one of them must be released under the same licence. The game is not affected, and the per-file list is in `data/licenses/FLAGS.md`.
**Everything else** — Natural Earth, USGS, NGA, and the remaining 221 flags — is public domain or CC0, with no obligation at all.

**OpenHistoricalMap** is CC0 — no attribution, no share-alike, nothing. It is the only historical boundary source with no obligation at all, which is why the surveyed outlines in `tools/data/ohm_borders.json` may ship while aourednik/historical-basemaps (GPL-3.0) remains a report a human reads.

**No historical boundary dataset is shipped or vendored.** `tools/check_map_history.py` reads one, GPL-3.0, as a report a person reads before editing this project's own province tables by hand. What ships is which country held which ground in a given year, at this project's raster resolution: a historical fact, not a copy of anyone's expression of it. The check fails if that dataset ever appears inside the repository, because the reasoning only holds while it stays outside.

data.name: Wikimedia Commons
data.license: Public domain, CC0 and OGL-om 1.0 — per file
data.attribution_text: Flag artwork from Wikimedia Commons. Per-file licences and required attribution: data/licenses/FLAGS.md.

data.name: OpenHistoricalMap
data.what: National outlines for the historical scenarios, at each scenario's own date

removed_data.name: GREG (Geo-referencing of Ethnic Groups), ETH Zurich
removed_data.why: No licence is offered. The download page asks only that the dataset be cited "when using the GREG data for your research" — a citation request under research framing, not a grant, and silent on redistribution or on shipping derived data in a game. GREG is itself a digitisation of the 1964 Soviet Atlas Narodov Mira, so ETH is in no position to sublicense the underlying work either; asking them could not have produced a usable answer.
removed_data.replaced_by: tools/data/ethnic_groups.json — project-authored country compositions from public-domain reference material, plus hand-drawn concentration boxes. See tools/generate_minorities.py.

removed_data.name: ACOR (oil and gas field polygons), ETH Zurich
removed_data.was: Oil field centroids behind the oil layer of resources.json
removed_data.why: Same shape of problem as GREG: no licence text, a citation requirement only, and the polygons are digitised from a 1982 atlas.
removed_data.replaced_by: tools/data/oil_fields.json — a project-authored list of named producing regions with play-balance weights. See load_oil_fields() in tools/overlay_real_data.py.

libraries.name: nanosvg
libraries.what: SVG parsing and rasterising for flags and symbols

libraries.name: stb_image / stb_image_write

fonts.name: GNU Unifont
fonts.what: CJK and fallback glyph coverage. Unifont is dual-licensed OFL 1.1 / GPLv2+ with a font-embedding exception; OpenDoctrines takes the OFL grant, under which the font may be bundled with and sold as part of a larger work provided it is not sold on its own.

art.name: SVG symbol set
art.what: Heraldic symbols used by the procedural flag generator
